findings: The cleaned dataset has 101,525 accidents; 26.2% are Fatal/Serious and 73.8% Slight, so the classes are imbalanced and accuracy alone would be misleading.
Number of vehicles is right-skewed: median 2, 95th percentile 3, maximum 17. These large crashes are real events, so they were kept and a log transform is used for modelling.
The share of Fatal/Serious accidents is highest at hour 4 (33.1%, n=634) and lowest at hour 8 (21.4%); the busiest hour for accidents is 17:00.
By speed limit, the severe share ranges from 22.4% (value 20.0) to 36.4% (value 60.0) among groups with at least 203 accidents.
By light-condition code, the severe share ranges from 23.4% (value 7) to 36.3% (value 6) among groups with at least 203 accidents.
By urban/rural code, the severe share ranges from 23.9% (value 1) to 30.9% (value 2) among groups with at least 203 accidents.
Weekend accidents are 28.5% severe versus 25.5% on weekdays.
The strongest linear correlation with the severe flag is latitude (r=+0.09); all correlations are weak-to-moderate and, being observational, do not show causation.
After cleaning, 'junction_control' has the most remaining missing values (43.8%); these are imputed inside the modelling pipeline (training data only).
